searchText: <@!425572898787426305> Question again(😂 sorry). Regarding the transition trigger, now the first `NewHead` event is regarded as the trigger for `PoW` -> `Transition`. However when the first `NewBlock` event received, the local chain needs to verify the block with new rules since it's the first PoS block. Can we use the first `NewBlock` event as the trigger in the implementation wise? Even if the block has been executed successfully we can't be sure that it's been processed successfully by consensus layer as there are other checks than executing the payload. While `NewHead` could be sent only if a block has been processed successfully from all points of view. What if an updated client code would listen and accept `NewHead` from the very beginning upon deployment? Wouldn't it be easier to get implemented? but the spec says `NewBlock message block is built on top of current head of the chain. The block becomes a new head if it’s been processed and considered as valid.` So, `NewBlock` doesn't mean the block will be the chain head? Depending on implementation in some cases the "valid block" information might not be enough to make a decision about the head. Let me remove this statement from the spec I was wrong about it **Merge Implementers' Call 3** is in 28 hours OK. So it's two steps procedure. (1) execute the block and persist if valid (2) switch head yes, this is correct fixed in the doc

However when the first `NewBlock` event received, the local chain needs to verify the block with new rules since it's the first PoS block. Can we use the first `NewBlock` event as the trigger in the implementation wise?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
Even if the block has been executed successfully we can't be sure that it's been processed successfully by consensus layer as there are other checks than executing the payload. While `NewHead` could be sent only if a block has been processed successfully from all points of view.

What if an updated client code would listen and accept `NewHead` from the very beginning upon deployment? Wouldn't it be easier to get implemented?

excerpts.author: garyrong
excerpts.content: but the spec says `NewBlock message block is built on top of current head of the chain. The block becomes a new head if it’s been processed and considered as valid.`

excerpts.author: garyrong
excerpts.content: So, `NewBlock` doesn't mean the block will be the chain head?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Depending on implementation in some cases the "valid block" information might not be enough to make a decision about the head. Let me remove this statement from the spec

excerpts.author: garyrong
excerpts.content: OK. So it's two steps procedure. (1) execute the block and persist if valid (2) switch head
